periods.label: Gujarat Sultanate to Mughal conquest
periods.summary: The Roza is built and enlarged: the saint's tomb (1445 to 1451), then Mahmud Begada's tank and family tombs, then the garden added in 1584.

periods.label: 1600 to 1899: early records
periods.summary: Few Roza-specific records are held. The earliest photographs and a measured plan date from the 1850s and 1860s.

periods.label: 1900 to 1999: gap in the record
periods.summary: No sourced local record for this century is held yet. This is a gap in this site's evidence, not evidence that nothing changed.

periods.label: 2000 to today: city expansion
periods.summary: Municipal merger, highway and transit works, town-planning schemes and census counts, recorded here as approvals, plans and milestones rather than finished change.

events.title: The saint dies; a tomb is ordered
events.text: Shaikh Ahmed Khattu Ganj Bakhsh died at Sarkhej in 1445. Sultan Muhammad Shah ordered a mausoleum and mosque built in his honour.

source.title: Sarkhej Roza, the Living Monument (Sahapedia)

events.uncertainty: The Roza committee's site gives the same year; some sources give 1446 for the death. Details of the saint's age are not used here.

events.title: The saint's tomb and mosque are completed
events.text: The mausoleum and mosque were completed in 1451 under Qutb-ud-din Ahmed Shah, the successor of Muhammad Shah.

source.title: Sarkhej Roza, the Living Monument (Sahapedia)

events.uncertainty: Corroborated by the Roza committee's site and Wikipedia.

events.title: Mahmud Begada enlarges the complex
events.text: During Sultan Mahmud Begada's reign the central tank was dug and a mausoleum for his family was built opposite the saint's tomb, making the Roza a royal retreat as well as a shrine.

source.title: Historic Values (Sarkhej Roza committee site)

events.uncertainty: No exact year for the tank or the tombs was found; only the reign (1458 to 1511, per Sahapedia) bounds the work.

events.title: Garden added after the Mughal conquest
events.text: Further additions, including a garden known as Fatehwadi, were made in 1584 to mark the defeat of the last Gujarat sultan by Mughal forces.

source.title: Sarkhej Roza, the Living Monument (Sahapedia)

events.uncertainty: Sahapedia and the Roza committee agree on 1584; Wikipedia names a different patron for the layout, which is not repeated here.

events.title: An early photograph of the Roza
events.text: A Thomas Biggs albumen print of Sarkhej Roza, held by the Rijksmuseum and marked public domain, dates from between about 1856 and 1866. It is among the earliest known views.

source.title: Gezicht op Sarkhej Roza bij Ahmedabad (Rijksmuseum)

events.uncertainty: The museum gives a date range, not a year. The image itself is not reproduced on this site; follow the link.

events.title: A measured plan of the Roza is published
events.text: A plan of Sarkhej Roza appears in the book 'Architecture at Ahmedabad, the Capital of Goozerat' (1866), later scanned by the British Library and shared on Wikimedia Commons with no known copyright restrictions.

source.title: File:Plan of Sarkhej Roza Ahmedabad1.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

events.uncertainty: The plan records the layout as surveyed in the 1860s; it has not been georeferenced, so it is not overlaid on the map.

events.title: The Roza's buildings are notified as protected monuments
events.text: Seven parts of the Roza (the Great Mosque, the Great Tank with the palace and harem, the pavilion and four tombs and rozas) are listed by the National Monuments Authority as centrally protected monuments in ASI's Vadodara Circle, each with a notification date of 27 May 1909. The Authority places them in its category of living monuments that receive many visitors and pilgrims.

source.title: National Monuments Authority: categorisation of centrally protected monuments, Vadodara Circle, ASI (Category VI, items 51 to 57)

events.uncertainty: The date comes from the Authority's categorisation list (file dated April 2023), not from the 1909 notification itself, which was not seen; the list gives no notification number. The protected and regulated area boundaries around the Roza are not published in this list and are not drawn.

events.title: Earthquake damage and restoration
events.text: The 2001 Gujarat earthquake badly damaged the Baradari at Sarkhej Roza, which the Archaeological Survey of India later restored.

source.title: Sarkhej Roza, the Living Monument (Sahapedia)

events.uncertainty: The restoration year is not given in the source.

events.title: Census 2001: Makarba and Sarkhej-Okaf
events.text: The 2001 census records Makarba as a census town of 18,047 people. Sarkhej-Okaf, a municipality with an outgrowth, is recorded in two parts: 23,412 people in Ahmadabad City taluka and 5,396 in Daskroi taluka, 28,808 in all.

source.title: Census of India 2001, Table C-01: Population by religious community, Gujarat (Office of the Registrar General)

events.uncertainty: Totals are the 'Total persons' column of the official table (town codes 40712000 and 40713000). Earlier versions of this page used Wikipedia's 18,090 and 23,086, which do not match the table. Sarkhej-Okaf's total includes its outgrowth. No 2011 count exists on these boundaries (see the evidence notes).

events.title: Makarba Municipality is included in the City of Ahmedabad
events.text: A state notification of 14 February 2006 includes the entire areas of seven municipalities in the limits of the City of Ahmedabad: Bodakdev, Makarba, Nava Odhav, Nikol, Vastrapur, Nava Naroda and Thaltej. These municipalities had been constituted by notifications of 10 August 2005.

source.title: Government of Gujarat, Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, Notification No. KV/25/2006/AMN/902006/410/P dated 14 February 2006 (copy hosted by AUDA)

events.uncertainty: Read from a scanned copy of the notification hosted by AUDA. The notification says government land in these areas does not vest in the corporation. It gives no boundary map.

events.title: Sarkhej-Okaf is merged into the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation
events.text: On 20 July 2006 the state government merged ten nagarpalikas, including Sharkhej-Okaf, and 30 gram panchayats into the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, according to a news report.

source.title: Gujarat urban development merges 10 nagarpalikas, 30 gram panchayats (OneIndia/UNI)

events.uncertainty: A news report of the announcement. The notification itself (No. KV/211/2006/AMN/902006/410/P, 20 July 2006) is hosted by AUDA, but the scanned copy omits Schedule A, which lists the municipalities, so Sarkhej-Okaf's inclusion is not yet confirmed from the notification. Other sources count 17 municipalities. Makarba was not part of this step: it was included separately on 14 February 2006.

events.title: Janmarg bus rapid transit opens in Ahmedabad
events.text: The Janmarg BRTS opened to the public on 14 October 2009 (Pirana to RTO junction), with the rest of phase one following on 25 December 2009. This is a city-wide milestone.

source.title: Janmarg (Wikipedia)

events.uncertainty: This does not show when buses reached Sarkhej or Makarba: the opening years of the Sarkhej-area routes were not found. No primary record was found (searched 2026-11-24): no AMC or Ahmedabad Janmarg Ltd document gives the opening date, and the chief minister's press note of 15 October 2009 and Wikipedia name different end points for the first corridor.

events.title: Six-laning of the S.G. Highway is approved
events.text: In February 2017 the Centre approved a plan to widen the 44 km Sarkhej-Gandhinagar highway to six lanes, with flyovers planned at several junctions between Sindhubhavan and Infocity.

source.title: Centre approves Rs 750 crore Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway 6-laning project (DeshGujarat)

events.uncertainty: A plan reported in the news. It says nothing about what was built or when, and the listed flyovers are not at Sarkhej itself. The cost differs between reports. No primary record was found (searched 2026-11-24): no PIB, Cabinet or MoRTH release for this approval turned up, and reports give 750, 847 and 867 crore.

events.title: Foundation stone laid for six-laning NH 147
events.text: On 24 September 2018 a foundation stone was laid for six-laning about 44 km of NH 147 (Sarkhej-Gandhinagar-Chiloda), including a 4.18 km elevated corridor between Sola Bhagwat and the Thaltej underpass.

source.title: Foundation stone laid for 44 km 6-lane conversion of Sarkhej-Gandhinagar-Chiloda highway (DeshGujarat)

events.uncertainty: A start-of-work ceremony, not completion. The elevated corridor is at the Gandhinagar end, not at Sarkhej. The cost is given inconsistently in the report. No primary record was found (searched 2026-11-24): no PIB or state press release for the ceremony turned up.

events.title: Changes to TP Scheme 204 (Makarba) are approved
events.text: The civic body approved changes to Town Planning Scheme 204 (Makarba), which covers about 1,121 hectares across Makarba, Okaf, Vejalpur and Ambli, after a freeze on construction approvals.

source.title: Ahmedabad civic body approves changes to Makarba TP scheme (Construction World)

events.uncertainty: The year is the article's publication date. AUDA's own scheme page was not checked, so the scheme number and area are not confirmed against a government record. No primary record was found (searched 2026-11-24): only news reports of the AMC town planning committee's approval; no state sanction or gazette reference.

tpSchemes.name: TP 84/A (Makarba)

source.title: AMC: History of Town Planning in Gujarat (PDF)

tpSchemes.note: Listed in AMC's published table. A proposal stage, not a built condition. Status and date are copied as displayed and are not asserted as current.

source.title: Town Plan Map: TP scheme listings (aggregator of government records)

alsoListed.note: Listed as 'Makarba - 84/A' and again as 'Makarba 84-A (AMC)', status Final. This differs from AMC's older table (preliminary, 2014): schemes advance through stages, so the newer listing is likely later, but neither is dated precisely.

tpSchemes.name: TP 84/B (Makarba)

source.title: AMC: History of Town Planning in Gujarat (PDF)

tpSchemes.note: A draft scheme was sanctioned in 2011 as listed. AMC also publishes point records for two Makarba plots under this scheme; these are not boundaries and are not reused here.

source.title: Town Plan Map: TP scheme listings (aggregator of government records)

alsoListed.note: Detail panel shows 51.64 ha, 49 original and 49 final plots, 31.21% deduction, prepared by Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation. The area conflicts with the 41.80 ha in AMC's table; the difference is unresolved.

source.title: AMC: History of Town Planning in Gujarat (PDF)

tpSchemes.note: Listed as refused, so it did not become an implemented scheme. The entry shows no date.

source.title: Construction World, news report

tpSchemes.note: Covers parts of Makarba, Okaf, Vejalpur and Ambli. The original draft also included Sarkhej. The area is from the news report.

tpSchemes.name: TP 26 (Makarba)

source.title: Town Plan Map: TP scheme listings (aggregator of government records)

tpSchemes.note: Appears twice in the aggregator, as 'Makarba - 26' (Preliminary TPS with TPO) and 'Makarba-26' (Preliminary). Not in AMC's table as reviewed. No area or date was recorded.

source.title: Town Plan Map: TP scheme listings (aggregator of government records)

tpSchemes.note: Listed under Sarkhej, Daskroi. Not in AMC's table as reviewed. No area or date was recorded.

visualRecord.author: Museeb fakih

gaps.need: The 1909 notification text and number, and the mapped protected and regulated areas around the Roza (heritage bye-laws under the AMASR Act, if notified)
gaps.why: Protected status, ASI circle and the notification date (27 May 1909) are now sourced from the National Monuments Authority's list, but the list gives no notification number and no boundaries, so no protection area is drawn.
gaps.whoCanProvide: Archaeological Survey of India; National Monuments Authority

gaps.need: The boundary and buffer zone of the UNESCO 'Historic City of Ahmadabad' property
gaps.why: The National Monuments Authority's Vadodara Circle list does not include the Roza's components among the monuments it groups under the 'Historic City of Ahmadabad' property (ref. 1551). That does not settle whether the Roza lies in a buffer zone; the nomination dossier was not reachable (HTTP 403).
gaps.whoCanProvide: UNESCO nomination dossier; AMC heritage cell

gaps.need: Sanctioned maps of each TP scheme (original and final) with a recorded coordinate system
gaps.why: Without them scheme boundaries, planned roads and earlier land use cannot be drawn or compared with today.
gaps.whoCanProvide: AUDA and AMC Town Planning departments (records request)

gaps.need: Dated land-use or built-up maps for the same area (for example Survey of India sheets, development plans, documented satellite classifications)
gaps.why: Needed for any built-up, green-cover or water-extent comparison; none is held.
gaps.whoCanProvide: Survey of India; AUDA development plans; a documented satellite analysis

gaps.need: Opening years and alignments of the S.G. Highway widening, the Sarkhej circle works, Sarkhej BRTS routes and the Ring Road
gaps.why: Only approvals and ceremonies are sourced; completion dates and geometry are not.
gaps.whoCanProvide: NHAI or the state Roads and Buildings Department, AMC, AUDA, Ahmedabad Janmarg Ltd

gaps.need: Census of India 2011 counts for Makarba and Sarkhej-Okaf on matching boundaries
gaps.why: The 2011 District Census Handbook (Part XII-B) has no row for either former town; Ahmedabad's wards are listed by number only, so none can be matched to the 2001 boundaries without the 2011 ward map. Two comparable years are needed before a population change can be charted.
gaps.whoCanProvide: Census of India (2001 PCA; 2011 ward delimitation map for Ahmadabad M Corp.); AMC (ward boundaries, Statistical Outline 2006-07 added areas)

gaps.need: Dated records of the Sarkhej tank's water level and extent, and of encroachment on the Roza complex
gaps.why: An 'about 29 to about 14 hectares' figure circulates but has no dates, so it is not charted. Open water within 500 m of the Roza is now charted from Landsat (1990 to 2024), but that is post-monsoon water in a circle, not the tank's outline or the complex's area, so it neither confirms nor dates that figure.
gaps.whoCanProvide: ASI, AMC, a dated survey or satellite analysis

gaps.need: Consented, anonymised recollections of change over time from residents and traders
gaps.why: No past-to-present testimony has been cleared for publication; none is invented.
gaps.whoCanProvide: The study's own interviews, once ethics approval and consent allow

gaps.need: Records of the Roza in the 18th to 20th centuries
gaps.why: No Maratha-era, colonial or independence-era sources specific to the Roza were found.
gaps.whoCanProvide: ASI conservation reports; Gujarat State Archives; academic studies

gaps.need: Reconcile each scheme's stage, date and area between AMC/AUDA records and aggregator listings (for example 84/B: 41.80 ha vs 51.64 ha)
gaps.why: The same scheme is described differently by different sources, so neither is shown as authoritative.
gaps.whoCanProvide: AUDA and AMC Town Planning departments
